newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares up on Washington summit.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares up on Washington summit.

text.p: After two sessions of sharp declines, Israeli shares turned higher on Monday amid hopes over a planned summit in Washington after violent clashes last week between Israelis and Palestinians.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares was up 1.72 points, or 0.93 percent, in early trading at 186.0 after tumbling 6.3 percent in the previous two sessions on last week's violence. The Maof index of blue chips rose 2.32 points or 1.2 percent to 195.40 points.

Eli Nahum, head of research at Zannex Securities, attributed the turnaround to Sunday's announcement by U.S. President Bill Clinton of a Middle East summit this week. "Once they set this meeting, the market became optimistic," said Nahum.

But it was not clear whether the meeting would be held. Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Monday was still mulling it over, suspicious that Israel will not give real guarantees at the summit to pursue previous peace agreements. And Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat has asked for a postponement on similar grounds, Palestinian official have said.
Rises were led by blue chip stocks, notably Koor industries , Bezeq Israel Telecom and Israel Chemicals , but small capitalisation stocks were also doing well.
"The market right now is green all over," said Nahum. Teva Pharmaceutiucal Industries, which rose strongly on Sunday, continued higher this morning on strong volume.

He warned, however, that the market's direction very much depended on the outcome of the Washington summit, which is supposed to include the leaders of Israel, the Palestinians, Jordan and maybe Egypt. "If the meeting is successful, it semms likely the positive trend will continue," Nahum said.
